title: Pre-1997 AGCD climate fits with three-year memory left a 2010-2019 runoff deficit at 70 Victorian gauges
abstract: We tested whether climatic memory accounts for a runoff deficit after the Millennium Drought. We added potential evaporation and the preceding three-year mean precipitation-minus-potential-evaporation term to seasonal rainfall regressions. We used CAMELS-AUS v2.03 with AGCD rainfall, 70 Victorian gauges and fits before 1997. In 2010-2019, memory changed the equal-gauge mean residual by +0.140 baseline error standard deviations, with a conditional 95% interval of -0.097 to +0.351. The remaining residual was -0.809, with interval -1.411 to -0.261. At 959 earlier chronological targets in 1982-1996, memory raised mean squared error by 1.54%. The interval for error reduction was -16.89% to +7.47%. The SILO rainfall check retained a negative point residual, but its interval reached zero. The result gives no clear prediction gain for this fixed three-year term. It does not exclude nonlinear storage, longer memory, or other climate effects. Shared weather, nested gauges, model form, selected records and source error limit inference. The package includes code, exact source and derived-evidence hashes, aggregate results, resampling draws, a numerical audit and a figure. External record-level data remain outside the signed publication.

display.caption: Fixed pre-1997 fits leave a 2010-2019 runoff deficit after three-year climatic memory is added. Error bars use spatial cells and shared three-year blocks, conditional on fitted models. Earlier prediction gain is uncertain.

citations.reason: We follow its published coverage sample, annual aggregation rule and seasonal design. We add climatic memory, potential evaporation, uncertainty and independent numerical checks. Source data overlap.
Its post-drought state result motivates a test of omitted climate memory. We do not retest its 2025 state labels.
CAMELS-AUS v2.03 external inputs, reused in place; exact files and hashes are preserved in provenance.json.
Prior climatic-wetness and runoff-state timing work. Our test freezes a different runoff relation before 1997.
